paper.title_en: On the Prospects of Using Cyclic Spectroscopy on Canonical Pulsars
paper.abstract_en: We use the cyclic figure of merit to determine the likelihood of achieving cyclic deconvolution for 2609 canonical pulsars, a population for which this technique has not previously been used. These pulsars have spin periods between 0.1 and 10 seconds and are surveyed across 15 different telescope-observing frequency combinations. We conclude that cyclic deconvolution will only be a viable method for pulse broadening function or phase retrieval recovery in a handful of canonical pulsars. Few, if any, pulsars pass the conservative threshold for a given telescope-frequency combination. We believe that the cyclic figure of merit does not accurately reflect our ability to use cyclic deconvolution on this population, instead showing a shortcoming of the measurement when observing canonicals at low observing frequencies. Still, it is reliable for MSPs and for canonicals at high observing frequencies. More promising is the prospect of using this technique to recover scintles for canonical pulsars; DSA and FAST are best-suited for this as judged by the number of sources where scintles may be resolved and S/N is sufficient. We suspect there may be more sources that would have large figures of cyclic merit, but insufficient S/N, at very low frequencies. We advocate for expansions of real-time cyclic spectroscopy backends for current and upcoming low frequency telescopes.
